claims.text: Varying the elemental percentages in HfNbTaTiZr HEA significantly influences its yield strength and ductility.
The Hf ratio has a particularly important influence on the mechanical properties of HfNbTaTiZr HEA.
Differences in atomic size and electronic structure cause composition-dependent changes in the mechanical properties.
A design-of-experiments approach can be used to systematically vary elemental percentages and assess their effects.
Changing elemental percentages alters lattice distortion in HfNbTaTiZr HEA.
Changing elemental percentages alters electronic bonding in HfNbTaTiZr HEA.
Changing elemental percentages alters dislocation dynamics in HfNbTaTiZr HEA.
Composition-induced changes in lattice distortion, electronic bonding, and dislocation dynamics produce variations in mechanical properties.
Increasing Hf content increases the yield strength of HfNbTaTiZr HEA.
Increasing Ti content increases the ductility of HfNbTaTiZr HEA.
Solubility and phase-stability limits bound the compositional range over which the hypothesis applies.
Tensile and compression testing of systematically varied compositions can measure composition-dependent yield strength and ductility.
DFT or molecular-dynamics simulations can be combined with mechanical testing to investigate the proposed underlying mechanisms.
